newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Paranagua port unions meet for strike vote.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Paranagua port unions meet for strike vote.

text.p: Unions at the key Brazilian port of Paranagua were meeting at the port to decide whether stevedores should take part in a nationwide strike scheduled for Friday, an official said.
"They are still meeting," said a spokeswoman at the Paranagua Stevedores' Union, adding that the reunion began at 0900 local/1200 GMT.
The port authority said the port was functioning normally and it was still not certain whether stevedores at Paranagua would call a stoppage for Friday.
"They are in a special situation here because the relationship between the port authority and the stevedores is very good," a port spokeswoman said.

In the event of a strike, the port is considering asking the workers that grain loading at its export terminal be maintained. But whether this proposal would be accepted was not yet certain, she said.

Stevedores at Santos port have been on strike since Wednesday over a ruling which allows company workers from steel mill Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) to operate Cosipa's private terminal at the port.
The strike is scheduled to spread to the national level on Friday, the National Stevedores' Union said.
